theorems: The full boxed Functional Choice schema has no equivalent finite list of original pure fixed-closed-type sentences over C.
The same nonfinite-equivalent-basis result holds for unboxed Functional Choice.
For every finite fragment of either schema, an actual constructed C-model satisfies that fragment and fails an explicitly quoted higher Choice instance.
Adjacent selector tower stages are strictly increasing; explicit separating models are provided.
Existing equivalences transfer the no-finite-basis conclusion to the tower-stage union, all-type diagonal Choice, and full boxed-selector schemas.
qualifications: Final boxed/unboxed nonfinite-basis declarations have no model-existence, countermodel, extraction, or finite-fragment-gap hypothesis. Such inputs are discharged by the construction and finitary derivation-support argument.
Equivalent bases may consist of arbitrary finite lists of sentences in the original pure language at fixed closed object types, not merely finite subsets of the Choice schema.
No additional object-language Infinity axiom or preservation of Infinity is asserted. The use of Nat in the ambient construction does not establish object-language Infinity after extraction.
This does not rule out finite strictly stronger sufficient packages implying full Choice, nor count an all-type axiom schema as one fixed-type sentence.

The proof uses ordinary classical semantic metatheory; the accepted axiom reports are propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice as individually listed. These are not additional object-language assumptions.
The recovered one-world general model need not retain the Boolean hierarchy carriers or their external cardinalities.
